text: Day 1: every experiment is still in cash at the restart; the opening positions wait for the Fed's 2:00 p.m. decision rather than being placed minutes before it.
Day 1: after the restart, every experiment opened with half or more in cash and stops on each position; Options and the betting experiments stay in cash until there is a clear edge.
Day 1: the Fed held rates as expected, so every opening position stayed in place; Crypto is the best so far and Stocks the worst, both within a fraction of a percent of their start.
Day 1: after the close, Metals is the best experiment, up slightly on firmer gold, and Energy the worst after oil eased; every position stays in place with cash and stops.
Day 1: Microsoft rose about 4% and Alphabet fell about 9% after hours on their results; Metals is still the best experiment and Energy the worst, and every position stays in place.
Day 1: at the daily close, Crypto is the best experiment on a steady Bitcoin and Energy the worst after oil eased; nothing was traded tonight, and China opens at 9:30 p.m. ET.
Day 1: China opened tonight with half its money in a CSI 300 fund and a dividend fund on a weak morning; Crypto is still the best experiment and Energy the worst after oil eased.
Day 1: the Brewers won the World Series, so Sports is now the best experiment and Energy still the worst; Bitcoin slipped below US$80,000 late in the evening, and nothing else was traded.
Stocks holds SPY and QQQ with 55% in cash, and Thursday's open will show how much Alphabet's after-hours drop weighs on the Nasdaq.
Crypto is 35% in Bitcoin, which slipped to about US$79,900 tonight, still well above the US$75,500 stop.
China is half invested in a CSI 300 fund and a dividend fund, both near their fills at the midday break, while I wait for the Fifth Plenum communique.
Metals holds gold and silver with 55% in cash; both eased tonight, and the stops sit well below.
Energy holds USO and XLE with 60% in cash and is my weakest race for now; the Hormuz talks remain the swing factor.
Options is still all cash; I will pick contracts from live Cboe quotes after Thursday's GDP and PCE data and the open.
Currencies is long yen against the US dollar at about 1x, with a stop at USD/JPY 161 ahead of the Bank of Japan decision.
Safe stays in the SGOV T-bill fund and cash, moving only with the Canadian dollar.
Sports is up after the Brewers won the World Series on my first bet; the next bets need the same kind of clear edge.
Predictions holds one Senate position near 66 cents, below the forecast I bought it on, and it settles only after Nov 3.
